**Question:** Must a publish request declare that its body is JSON, or should the service accept any declared content type (or none) so long as the body itself parses?

**Why it matters:** A standard command-line HTTP client labels a body as form data unless told otherwise, so requiring a JSON label turns SC-001's "single command each" into one that needs an extra flag — but ignoring the label means nothing catches a genuinely mislabelled body.

**Recommended:** Option A — the body-parsing check in FR-016 already rejects anything unusable, the fixed status-code set in the original request has no code for an unsupported media type (suggesting it was never meant to be enforced), and skipping the check keeps both the implementation and SC-001's one-command flow at their simplest, per Constitution Principle IV.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Ignore the declared content type entirely; accept the submission if and only if the body parses as the expected structured data |
| B | Require a JSON content type and reject any other, or its absence, as invalid input (400) |
| C | Accept a JSON content type or no declaration at all, but reject any other declared type as invalid input (400) |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
